business_problem: Siemens Healthineers needed to speed up radiation-oncology model development and reduce the time clinicians spend contouring organs at risk so treatment planning could scale with rising cancer demand.
solution_summary: Siemens Healthineers uses its Sherlock AI supercomputer to industrialize machine-learning development for radiation oncology, especially the organ-contouring step that slows treatment planning. Sherlock combines NVIDIA HGX-1 and HGX-2 servers loaded with NVIDIA Tesla V100 GPUs, NVLink interconnects, 3 petabytes of NVMe storage, and a 100 Gbps Mellanox InfiniBand fabric so researchers can keep GPUs saturated and run more than 600 deep-learning experiments each day. The cluster trains AI models behind syngo.via RT Image Suite, including AutoContouring models built on more than 4.5 million images. Once trained, those models automatically outline 47 organs for radiation-oncology workflows, giving clinicians faster starting points for therapy planning while the same platform supports more than 45 approved AI applications across the broader imaging portfolio.
